title: Shuto Orizari residents and students’ public-transport protest
location: Skopje: gathering at the old post office and City of Skopje offices
scope: One-day public protest; sources describe people moving to City offices, with other residents already there.
organizer: Shuto Orizari residents and students; High School Students’ Union joined the call
threshold_50_evidence: No attendance number is reported. The approximately 40,000 Shuto Orizari residents affected is a population estimate, not protesters.

start_date.summary: Both reports date the protest to 22 November 2024.

location.summary: RFE/RL describes gathering at the old post office and moving to City offices; MIA places the protest at City of Skopje offices.

organizer.summary: Residents and students; high school students joined the call.

demands.summary: Restore bus routes serving Shuto Orizari and improve transit; free transit for students in private schools.

participants_original.summary: No attendance count. MIA’s 40,000 figure describes residents affected, not protesters.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Threshold cannot be assessed without simultaneous attendance data.

state_target.summary: Demands addressed to City of Skopje and its mayor regarding public transit service.

state_response.summary: City issued a response after the protest, criticizing political manipulation; this does not establish accommodation of the service demands.

notes: The state reserve-fuel decision mentioned by MIA preceded the protest; it is not coded as a protest response. City response reported by RFE/RL is coded as ignore/non-accommodation only.
open_questions: Is there contemporaneous evidence of at least 50 people simultaneously at the 22 November protest? The 40,000 figure refers to residents affected by transit service, not demonstrators.

Do the captured sources establish that the 22 November gathering was part of a broader public-transport campaign with other distinct actions, or should it remain a single dated event? If other actions are identified, what evidence connects them as one campaign rather than separate events?
